subject: bicycle
pitch: A vintage Dutch city bicycle in mint green. Tall upright handlebars with cream grips and a silver bell, a brown leather saddle with springs, chrome mudguards, a chain guard, a wicker basket on the front filled with sunflowers and a baguette, and whitewall tyres.
reasoning:
I need to be careful about which SDK APIs I actually trust, since I'm not fully certain of exact signatures. I'll stick to safer builder calls like part, joint, rod, capsule, using options like at, bone, aim, and frame rather than riskier untested methods.

I'm planning the bicycle's geometry: wheel radius, axle positions along Z, wheelbase length, and a joint hierarchy for frame, wheels, handlebar, and pedal crank, with explicit parent relationships between joints. I'll write a helper function that builds a tube/cylinder between two points by computing orientation from a quaternion and attaching it to the correct bone.

For the wheels, I'm combining a torus for the black tyre with thin ring geometries positioned and rotated to sit flush on either side as whitewall accents, oriented so they face outward along the X axis.

Now I'm planning the chrome rim torus, the 16 alternating spokes connecting hub to rim, and setting up the wheel as a group that rotates about X for animation. Then I'm sketching the bike frame itself — a mint-colored step-through "omafiets" style with a curved seat tube running from the bottom bracket up to the seat, plus the head tube placement.

Still working out the swooping down tube curve and chain stays...

Continuing to lay out the rest of the bike: Dutch-style swept-back handlebars rising from the stem with cream-colored grip cylinders at the ends, plus a small bell on top near the stem.

I'm now positioning a front basket on a rack attached to the steerer, above the front wheel, sized and placed to clear the tire and mudguard, and shaping it as a tapered frustum using a four-sided rotated cylinder geometry with double-sided material to leave it open on top.

I'll build the basket's wicker texture from vertical stake-like boxes and horizontal ring bands in brown tones, add a thick rim tube around the top edge, and fill it with sunflowers made from brown cylinder discs, flattened yellow petal cones, and green stems, plus a tan baguette with scored darker boxes sticking out of the basket.

For the sunflower geometry, I'm defining a helper that computes an orientation matrix mapping a local Y-axis to the flower's facing normal, then arranging 14 petals radially in two offset layers around a cylindrical disc using cone shapes rotated and translated outward before applying that orientation transform.

Now I'm working on the stem as a tube curving from the flower down to the basket, and the saddle as scaled, flattened sphere shapes (a wider rear, narrower nose) to mimic leather, plus planning helical tube geometry for the stirrup springs using a Catmull-Rom curve.

I'm placing the spring coils near the rear of the saddle, adding a chrome seatpost tube connecting the seat tube to the saddle base, and nudging the saddle's vertical position and radius so everything lines up properly above the frame.

Now I'm moving on to the crank and pedal assembly, positioning the bottom bracket joint for proper ground clearance and sketching the chainring as a chrome cylinder with a chain guard.

The rear sprocket cylinder sits hidden inside the guard, so I can skip detailing it. For the crank, I'm placing opposing arms from the BB with the right arm angled forward and the left angled back, each ending in a small dark pedal box.

For mudguards, I'm figuring out how to make partial chrome arcs over the wheels using a scaled torus geometry — stretching it along the axle axis with a matrix scale and rotating it into place to form a curved band.

I'm sizing the mudguard torus so its radius sits just outside the tyre, tuning the tube width and segment count so it reads as a thin curved ribbon rather than a bulky ellipsoid. I'll skip the rear rack for now but consider adding a small rear light and kickstand for extra detail.

I'm positioning the headlamp as a small chrome sphere near the fork crown, then working out the basket placement and support rods so they clear the headlamp and wheel without overlapping, checking the z and y spans to keep everything proportioned against the front wheel and mudguard heights.

Now I'm defining the color palette for the frame—mint, cream, brown, chrome, black, wicker tones, yellow, and green—and setting up the joint hierarchy starting from a root frame joint near the origin.

Setting up child joints...

Still writing geometry helpers...

Still plotting frame geometry...

Still plotting handlebar curve points...

Placing the bell silver with a domed top and mount tube, then moving to the basket construction with vertical stakes along the front/back and side faces and horizontal rails in alternating rows around the perimeter.

For the sunflowers, I'm positioning five of them inside the basket with heads rising above the rim, tilted outward and angled upward, each with a stem running down into the basket; I'm sizing the disc and petals to form roughly a 0.2 diameter head, though I want to shrink that slightly for better proportion.

I'm also adding a single flattened green leaf per stem, randomly rotated for variety, and now working out where to place a baguette poking out of the basket at an angle, adjusting its endpoints to get a realistic length around 0.6 units.

For the baguette geometry, I'm using a capsule along a chosen axis with small radius, then scattering a few darker cream-colored score marks along its surface, offsetting each one perpendicular to the axis so they sit visibly on top rather than embedded inside.

I'm writing a helper function to orient geometry from a default Y-axis direction to any target direction using a quaternion, so I can reuse it for baguette, mudguard, and other angled parts.

Now I'm positioning a small red rear light at the end of the rear mudguard arc, checking the wheel's center and radius to make sure the light sits at the correct trailing point without being hidden by the mudguard's curved coverage.

Setting the front guard arc from about 50° to 170°, then placing a small rear light box near the rear guard's lower edge, and starting to position the kickstand tube.

I'm now laying out the drivetrain on the right side, with the chain guard box running from the bottom bracket to the rear axle and the crank arms extending forward and backward from the axle, each ending in a pedal box.

I'm writing the helper function for building tube geometry, converting start/end points into a cylinder oriented along the vector between them using quaternion rotation, then translating it to the midpoint.

For box-like guards I orient them similarly using a quaternion derived from the Z-axis, then finally return the completed root object.
